ateret-zekenim/2:_: A little in Torah. So wrote Mahari Weil from that which we learn in first chapter Rav Ashi was sitting before R' Kahana; he said why did the rabbis not come to the beit midrash etc.; he said they are busy with the Purim meal — we learn the Purim meal pushes aside Torah study; nevertheless since they expounded "this is Torah" — mitzvah to engage in Torah before the meal and it protects him that no mishap occur at the meal — end of his words.
baer-heitev/1:_: rejoice. Even on the night of the 14th Avodat HaTumah, and so Knesset HaGedolah and Levush: Shabbat clothes too from evening — I found so in Sedei Chemed, and thus: "and his house shall be filled with lit candles and a set table and spread bed."
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) and sleep. Some say he did not know to calculate cursed is Haman in gematria blessed is Mordechai. Taz wrote in my humble opinion it appears to explain a person must give praise to the Blessed One for double good He did for us: first the punishment He brought on Haman, and had Mordechai not been blessed but saved with all Israel we would have been satisfied; rather He blessed Mordechai with very great honor and extra good — therefore he said one must become intoxicated until he does not know our superiority of cursed is Haman which is his humiliation to blessed is Mordechai which is our second superiority — see there.
baer-heitev/3:א: (א) The miracles. And if he forgot about the miracles in Grace after Meals they return him, for he may not eat without it — Shelah, Rashal, Mateh Moshe. Taz and Magen Avraham wrote this is specifically the first meal he eats on Purim, for the main reason is he has obligation of his meal that day as written "days of feasting and joy"; if so the first meal he eats that day with which he fulfills Purim meal — we need not hang the law on what we call the meal after Minchah the Purim meal; if he already ate a first meal that day they do not return him — see there. In this vein he wrote in name of Maharal of Prague he ruled unlike Shelah and Maharshal, rather when he reaches haRachaman he says haRachaman He will do miracles for us — see siman 682.
baer-heitev/3:ב: (ב) First. See siman 488 seif 10 from what is written, and so in Mordechai: on parchment he would eat Purim meal on erev Purim, pray, spread a cloth and recite kiddush, and in Grace after Meals say on the miracles — end of his words; in Mateh Moshe and Minhagim they wrote since he did not pray Maariv it implies if he prayed he again does not say on the miracles — so too Shelah and Maharil in responsum siman 56; therefore it appears he should bless Grace after Meals first and then pray Maariv to remove himself from dispute and also lest he become drunk and not bless Grace after Meals. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/4:א: (א) Meat. Cooked fit for eating — Maharil; the same for drink — Shelah. One who sends money, clothing and vessels for portions — if he can sell them immediately to buy for the meal need — Leket Yosher ch. 2 siman 163. From words of Baal Turei Even siman 111 it implies somewhat he does not fulfill — see there Yad Aharon. I was in doubt one who sent his friend for portions a treif chicken and he did not know and they ate it, and later on Purim day itself it became known it was treif — whether he fulfilled mishloach manot obligation or not — see in Sefer Motzal MeEsh siman 61. I was further in doubt one who sent his friend abroad two portions, or two gifts to two poor people before Purim, and on Purim itself they certainly reach him — whether he fulfills or not: do we say since when he sent he was not yet obligated he does not fulfill, or perhaps since on Purim itself which is time of obligation they reached his hand he fulfills? See Yad Aharon whose view leans he fulfills properly in this — see there; one who sent his friend fish and egg on it or bread with face smeared with egg — doubt whether he fulfills mishloach manot — Edut B'Yaakov siman 92 see there; see Kanfei Nesharim.
baer-heitev/4:ג: (ג) A woman. I did not see women careful about this; perhaps specifically widows, but a woman who has a husband — her husband sends on her behalf to several people; nevertheless one should be stringent — Magen Avraham. It appears to me one who eats at his friend's table and prepared nothing for him is exempt from mishloach manot, and so somewhat in Rashi regarding they exchange their meals reciprocally; see Taz s.k. 3; nevertheless requires study and good to be stringent — Magen Avraham. He wrote in Sedei Chemed: one should gather all household members and friends, for if a person sits alone he cannot rejoice properly — so too Rashi on verse mishpacha u'mishpacha.
beer-hagolah/2:ב: (ב) There are those who explain blessed is Mordechai and cursed is Haman are gematriot of din and din, and one must drink so much until he cannot intend the number.
beer-hagolah/3:ב: (ב) Hagahot Maimoniot in chapter 2 Laws of Megillah in name of Rambam and Orach Chayyim in name of R' Yehuda of Korbeil.
beer-hagolah/3:ג: (ג) Tur in name of his father the Rosh.
beur-hagra/2:א: (א) s.k. 2 obligated etc. There one is obligated etc., meaning between vengeance of Haman and greatness of Mordechai — and this is what is written greatness vengeance that was given etc.; and they said greatness of knowledge, and since knowledge was removed he did not know etc.
beur-hagra/2:ד: (ד) And the practice is to do etc. Mateh Moshe s.k. 5 in name of Turei Even, and they extend drinking mostly until Minchah, and it is forbidden to begin before Minchah.
beur-hagra/2:ו: (ו) And he is obligated in feasting etc. as it is said the two days etc. Darkei Moshe in name of Minhagim; but in gemara five chapter 2 mishnah feasting and joy refers only each eats his day — see Rashi there d.h. lo nitzrecha etc.
beur-hagra/3:א: (א) s.k. 63 and if he began etc. as in Ne'ilah prayer, though for Rav in Yoma ch. 7 and for Tanna Kamma ch. 8 that one prays at night — see Rosh there in name of Yerushalmi; nevertheless he prays that of Shabbat as written in chapter 2 of Shabbat Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat etc., and though Rav does not hold R' Yehudah ben Lakish not because of night.
beur-hagra/3:ב: (ב) For after beginning etc. The main thing is whatever extends the breath of Shabbat or falls on it we mention that of Shabbat, therefore on Shabbat night he prays two of Shabbat and so mentions in Grace after Meals of Shabbat as Tosefta, and so in Ne'ilah mentions of Shabbat since he has not yet prayed Maariv and Shabbat sanctity still; not so one who prays two of weekday since he already prayed first of weekday — per this there is no difference whether he began, for even if he did not begin as above. Per Yerushalmi who finishes at night one could say we follow the beginning; but for our gemara at end of Yoma that even to begin at night is a dispute, since it says one may not immerse and as above.
beur-hagra/3:ג: (ג) There is who. As written in chapter 4 of Berachot: he erred and did not pray Minchah on erev Shabbat etc. on Shabbat he prays two of weekday, and in chapter erev Pesach they finished first cup and bless on it Grace after Meals, and they said in Tosefta of Berachot he mentions of Shabbat in Grace after Meals though it is a weekday meal — clearly we follow now; and s.k. first holds prayer is only makeup since Minchah time passed and he separates in the first but in Grace after Meals he blesses on what he ate from before and since he has not yet prayed weekday he says me'ein hame'orah. Maharil siman 56, meaning to answer the Rosh's second difficulty who challenged from that Tosefta that case is different since Shabbat already entered unlike here where all this he has not yet prayed Shabbat sanctity upon him.
beur-hagra/4:ב: (ב) One must send. As written days of feasting and joy and sending etc., and it refers to all of them; and they said there "days" is written.
biur-halacha/2:א: (א) A person is obligated etc. — one could ask how did Chazal obligate what is mentioned in Torah and Prophets in several places that intoxication is a great stumbling block; one could say because all miracles done for Israel in days of Ahasuerus were through feasting, for initially Vashti was removed through feasting and Esther came, and so the matter of Haman and his fall was through feasting, therefore the sages obligated to become intoxicated enough that the great miracle be remembered through wine drinking; nevertheless all this is for the mitzvah and not to prevent [Eliyahu Rabbah].
biur-halacha/2:ב: (ב) Until he does not know etc. — thus Meiri: a person must increase joy on this day in eating and drinking until he lacks nothing; nevertheless we are not commanded to become drunk and diminish ourselves from joy of mitzvah, for we were not commanded joy of frivolity and foolishness but joy of pleasure reaching love of the Blessed One and thanks for miracles He did for us — see there what he explains gemara words. Thus Chayei Adam: since the entire miracle was through wine, therefore sages obligated intoxication and at least to drink more than usual to remember the great miracle; indeed one who knows about himself he will treat a mitzvah lightly in Grace after Meals or will not pray Minchah or Maariv or will behave lightly — better he not become drunk and all his actions for the sake of the mitzvah — end of his words.
biur-halacha/4:ב: (ב) Or kinds of foods etc. — in Turei Even he is in doubt if he sent two portions to one poor person whether he can count them for two to fulfill mishloach manot, for the poor too is included in ish lere'ehu, and to fulfill matanot laevyonim; if he gave another gift to one poor person did he fulfill or not — Gra brought this in his chiddushim. Peri Chadash wrote city of doubt surrounded — send the portions on the 14th which is for most of the world; see Peri Megadim who doubts this.
chatam-sofer/3:_: (there in Hagahah) and if he sends. NB see these laws what Peri Chadash wrote and in responsa ch. same Orach Chayyim siman 196 [there he wrote on Peri Chadash's words who doubted Rama who ruled if he sent portions to his friend and he did not want to receive, since he forgave him he fulfills; Peri Chadash wrote I do not know from where this is. Behold in Korban Netanel first chapter of Megillah he answered Peri Chadash from gemara Nedarim daf 63b that one can permit his vow not through a sage by saying behold I am as if I was accepted — the same here likewise, and they justified Rama's words. I say the gaon did not see what Ran wrote in name of Yerushalmi there 24a that it refers to stam and R' Meir and rabbis dispute whether giver's intent is for his own honor or recipient's honor, but if giver's intent is for his own honor it does not help by saying behold I am as accepted; if so Peri Chadash wrote well from where for Rama, for intent of mishloach manot instituters was for sender's need or for whom it was sent. I saw two reasons in Tosafos Yom Tov: wrote so there be profit for feast hosts perhaps his meal will not suffice, behold his friend helps him — see there; one could say even if he has much, nevertheless they instituted thus not to shame one who lacks as we say at end of tractate Taanit; if so as if he truly lacks enough his forgiveness is nothing; if he has anyway he should not forgive because of not shaming. But in Sefer Manot HaLevi it is written to increase peace and friendship — opposite narrow mitzvah scattered and divided etc.; if so one could say since he sent and showed affection he already fulfilled even though this one forgives — Peri Chadash wrote well from where for Mahari Weil and Rama to decide this. See there further law whether a woman is obligated in mishloach manot like a man, and see there what he wrote on Peri Chadash's words].
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: Seif 2: a person must become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordechai. NB see what I wrote to explain this in my works on Orach Chayyim year 549 letter 224 and in derush for parashat Zachor year 553 in chiddushei Kehillat Yaakov — see there wondrous explanation with God's help; examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (there seif 4) he must send his friend two portions etc. NB I was in doubt regarding mishloach manot: if he sends a sick person something forbidden that is permitted for him to eat, such as stam yayinam for a patient without danger, or another d'rabbanan prohibition, or a Torah prohibition for a dangerously ill patient — whether he fulfills mishloach manot if we follow the recipient and behold it is fit for eating, or we follow the giver and for him it is not fit. This can be resolved from the verse itself from what is written "and sending of portions ish lere'ehu" — the word ish is extra and it would suffice "and sending portions lere'ehu", and as Ezra wrote "and they sent portions to one not his friend"; since it says ish lere'ehu necessarily intent is portions ish fit for this one he sends to his friend, but what is not fit for him also for his friend he does not fulfill. Yet one could doubt: if both are sick and permitted to eat forbidden things and the sender has one permitted portion and one forbidden and his friend has nothing — if he sends the permitted to his friend he must eat the forbidden — what shall he do? In general certainly we say your life takes precedence and he eats the permitted and gives his friend the forbidden, for my question is in mishloach manot on Purim since I raised that mishloach manot sender must send what is fit for him — do we say if he eats the permitted then the forbidden is not fit for him since he has permitted, then he does not fulfill mishloach manot, and since in the end the forbidden will be eaten, better he eat the forbidden and send the permitted to his friend and fulfill mishloach manot; or do we say in any case your life takes precedence and he eats the permitted even though he does not fulfill mishloach manot — like this case Rava needs, requires study, examine well. (there seif 4 in Hagahah) and if he sends portions to his friend and he does not wish to receive or forgives — he does not fulfill etc. NB see in my works on Orach Chayyim year 561 in responsum to Krakow community who bought place in Laws of Yom Kippur siman 218 what he wrote on this matter relevant here — see there and examine.
eshel-avraham/2:_: paying. See Rosh Sukkah daf 45 and Tosafot Yoreh Deah siman 344.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (ב) Even when it falls on Friday. Meaning he eats a meal from before a third meal; nevertheless the wise person's eyes are in his head that day to diminish somewhat his eating by day to make room for the Purim night meal, and he sets his table on Friday night of the 14th.
machatzit-hashekel/4:_: (s.k. 4) Torah scholar. It appears to me his intent etc., and see what is written siman 694. He challenged there Magen Avraham: behold we say in Pesachim daf 68 Mar brei d'Ravina would sit in fast all year except Shavuot and Purim and Yom Kippur — and they disputed its explanation: one says all year he would fast if a bad dream befell him he would fast — Torah scholar — except these three days that even a Torah scholar does not fast; then it is proven even a Torah scholar may not fast these three days. But one says simply he fasted all year day by day except these three days; then it does not refer to Torah scholar at all and there is no proof not to fast Torah scholar these three days. Behold above siman 694 he wrote one may not fast Torah study on erev Purim — therefore he holds like explanation one, and here he wrote one may fast Torah scholar on Purim — see that he holds like explanation two; behold two contradictory matters, and see what is written there Magen Avraham; therefore he wrote here Rama's intent is to fast until after Minchah, for thus Hagahot Rashba permitted above for all explanations — see there and also siman 552. See Rosh siman 570 as should read, meaning there is explained dispute of poskim whether a vow fell and therefore he concludes there he may annul his vow and not fast.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) And in meal one — unlike one who says he must eat also at night like Megillah; Bach wrote nevertheless one should eat at night even when it falls on Friday as written in Hagahah.
magen-avraham/2:א: (א) Rather he should drink more etc. Some say he did not know to calculate cursed is Haman in gematria blessed is Mordechai.
magen-avraham/2:ג: (ג) And most of the meal etc. That they do not practice making it in the morning is because they are busy with mishloach manot as we find end of chapter 8 of Chullin they would not increase meal on first Yom Tov of Sukkot because they were busy with sukkah and lulav [Turei Even].
magen-avraham/3:א: (א) He says on the miracles. And if he forgot on the miracles in Grace after Meals they return him, for he may not eat without it [Shelah, Rashal in name of R' Yehuda Pollak, Mateh Moshe]; nevertheless his words require study, for is he better than prayer which is obligatory and nevertheless they do not return him — all the more in Grace after Meals; therefore it appears if he already ate one meal that day they do not return him, for if he wishes he need not eat more; as Beit Yosef siman 488 in name of Tosafos — see there; and though Rashal did not write so, it appears what is written main law according to halacha, for per law it appears we never return him, for we did not find he must eat bread on Purim and he can exempt himself with one kind of delicacies; therefore in this case where he already ate it is simple not to return him and concern for doubtful blessing is void; and so in Mordechai: on parchment he ate Purim meal on erev Purim, prayed, spread cloth and kiddush, in Grace after Meals says on miracles — end; in Mateh Moshe and Minhagim they wrote since he did not pray Maariv it implies if he prayed he again does not say on miracles — so Shelah and Maharil responsum 56; therefore it appears he blesses Grace after Meals first then prays Maariv to remove dispute and also lest he become drunk and not bless Grace after Meals.
magen-avraham/4:ב: (ב) Two portions etc. It appears for poor people they were strict to give to two poor, for they can divide — not so for a rich person when he gives to one; it appears one who eats at his friend's table and prepared nothing is exempt from mishloach manot, and so somewhat Rashi regarding exchanging meals reciprocally; nevertheless requires study (see what is written siman 681 s.k. 6) and good to be stringent.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (א) (4) Between cursed is Haman — this is the first humiliation when great vengeance was taken from him, and further good beyond this is greatness of Mordechai whom the Holy One blessed be He blessed that he rose to supreme head; behold before he became drunk he certainly gave thanks to the Blessed One for the two goods, and therefore they said he should not cease giving thanks for this in joy until he comes to not distinguishing anymore between this good and that. See Eliyah Rabbah: nevertheless one should be careful regarding Grace after Meals and hamotzi blessing and Grace after Meals, and let it be joy of mitzvah; see Peri Megadim who wrote matter of Purim meal and matanot laevyonim and mishloach manot perhaps require intent for mitzvah sake.
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (א) (15) He says al hanissim in Grace after Meals etc. — and if he forgot to say al hanissim, some say they return him and some say they do not return him, and doubtful blessings lenient; specifically the first meal he eats that day, but the second meal he eats after Minchah called Purim meal and he already ate one meal that day — again all agree they do not return him, rather when he reaches haRachaman he says haRachaman He will do miracles for us etc. When Purim falls on erev Shabbat and his meal extends to night he must mention of now, namely v'ratsah; how then say on miracles which are contradictory; and since mention of al hanissim is not so weighty, therefore he says only that of Shabbat. All this even when he has not yet prayed, and especially if he prayed earlier certainly not worth mentioning al hanissim in Grace after Meals as below.
peri-megadim/3:_: And the practice is — Taz; and in siman 488 note 6 the same here when Purim falls on erev Shabbat and his meal extends to night he says on miracles and v'ratsah — see there in Magen Avraham note 10 it will be explained further.
peri-megadim/4:_: Kinds of foods — Taz; and it implies superficially raw meat is permitted; Peri Chadash Chayyim: one should not send — behold slaughtered live one may send as it appears; in Magen Avraham 1 in name of Maharil specifically cooked portions implies it should be fit to honor per place and time; in our chiddushim we wrote from this.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: and sleep. Avodat HaTumah; see in Siddur Amudei Shamayim who wrote his father the gaon in his youth practiced to fulfill the statement literally. One weak by nature (or who becomes foolish until he may come through this to improper act or words) should not drink more than enough, and proof to the matter Ribi"a — examine end of his words. His intent in what he wrote Ribi"a is acronym R' Yehudah bar Ilai, meaning R' Yehudah bar Ilai said in Yerushalmi he drinks only from Pesach to Pesach and girds his temples etc. — implies on Purim he did not drink since his drinking harmed his bodily health.
turei-zahav/2:א: (א) A person must become intoxicated etc. Many wish to answer and explain what the intent is here and it was not settled; in my humble opinion to explain thus: a person must give praise to the Blessed One for double good He did for us — first punishment He brought on Haman, and had Mordechai not been blessed but saved with all Israel we would have been satisfied; rather He blessed Mordechai with very great honor and extra good — therefore he said one must become intoxicated until he does not know our superiority of cursed is Haman which is his humiliation to blessed is Mordechai which is our second superiority; the intent from saying until he does not know implies before his intoxication he knew and gave thanks for this — they intended he should not cease giving thanks for this in joy until he comes to not distinguishing anymore, and then he is exempt from this in my humble opinion.
turei-zahav/2:ב: (ב) And some say he need not become drunk etc. The statement of Rava in gemara until he does not know etc. is rejected by this statement, since in gemara he brings on this Rabbah who slaughtered R' Zeira — we learn from gemara conclusion one should not do so much; Beit Yosef in name of Ran in name of R' Efraim.
turei-zahav/4:ב: (ב) Exchange with his friend. In gemara they say Abbaye bar Avin and R' Chanina bar Avin exchange their meals reciprocally; Ran explained neither was able to send and leave for himself, therefore each sends his meal to the other to eat Purim meal and fulfill mishloach manot; this way is written here; Rashi explained they exchange meals — this one eats with that one on Purim this year and second year his friend feasts with him; Beit Yosef challenged Rashi's explanation: if so they did not fulfill mishloach manot ish lere'ehu; you could say they sent portions ish lere'ehu — what does it teach? End of his words; in my humble opinion for Rashi it was a novelty they said explicitly this one will eat with this one and then reverse, and one could say it was like a loan and there is no manot here since gift specifically — it teaches nevertheless they fulfilled, meaning this year this one fulfilled by inviting his friend and his friend sent to another person, and second year the reverse; but one must be exact: why did Rashi not explain truly all on one year and both fulfilled? Perhaps one could say then it was truly complete loan since all see immediately he receives payment and there was condition between them — not so if in two years it would not appear like payment this year and not that; example for this we find (Yoreh Deah) siman 170 s.k. 2 in Hagahah: one should not say to his friend come eat with me what you fed me, for it is like paying his debt and appears as if he loaned him, and concern he will feed him more and there is interest; but permitted to say come eat with me and I will eat with you another time, and permitted to eat with him even a greater meal — end. Behold at second eating it is forbidden to mention it is payment — so too here then it was loan in my correct opinion.
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 4; see beginning siman 570 we do not hold so as should read, and see there one may annul his vow; for Rambam it does not apply at all.
yad-ephraim/3:_: In Taz s.k. 1 a person must become intoxicated etc. Many wish to answer and explain what the intent is here etc.; to me the younger it was explained in a night vision that the intent is the main obligation of the feast is he be steeped in joy as written "and wine gladdens a person's heart", and because he be steeped in joy the joy of the Blessed One is his strength and he gives thanks and hallel to the Blessed One for the miracle from breadth of heart, per what they said gather wine etc.; therefore he should not become drunk more than enough that his mind be confused and he not recognize the force of the miracle at all; thus he said a person must become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know etc. — this "until" is and not "until" in general, meaning great is obligation of drinking here to become intoxicated until the boundary he does not know etc.; from this boundary onward it is nullification of intent of obligation the sages obligated to become intoxicated in order to give hallel and thanks, for since his mind is so confused he does not know between cursed is Haman etc. — clearly he has no mind and understanding to praise and glorify the force of the miracle; I considered it in the morning and saw it is correct and settled what gemara relied on the incident of Rabbah and R' Zeira who made Purim meal together etc., which superficially is an act to contradict; some poskim wrote the intent is from this one learns the halacha is not like Rava here; per what is written one could say on the contrary it brings support, for what they obligated days of feasting and joy has a boundary not to become drunk more than enough, for we precede Rabbah and R' Zeira etc.; and since they did not guard from crossing the boundary the matter came to danger — therefore one must be careful not to become intoxicated only until this boundary he does not know etc. and not cross.
levushei-serad/4:_: s.k. 4 and Or Zaru'a 493 — should read siman 570; see Magen Avraham s.k. 8.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (א) And at the feast etc. and Gemara etc. also at night etc. — meaning night of the 14th as Magen Avraham small seif 2 — similar to Megillah and Shabbat offering and its day. Bach brought proof also night of 14th has some mitzvah from Megillah 7: R' Eliezer sat before R' Kahana on Purim evening, sages didn't come — "perhaps busy with Purim feast" — "can't eat in the evening?" — "don't hold like Rav: Purim feast eaten at night didn't fulfill" etc.; if night of 14th also has some feast mitzvah only main feast must be by day — one could say R' Kahana erred thinking permitted reverse — main feast at night, day only partial without needing bustle — until we answered Rav's Purim feast etc.; otherwise no mitzvah at all on night 14th — presumably custom not to enlarge night feast — how could R' Kahana err so much that Purim feast at night fulfills? See there.
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (ד) And above siman 568 seif 5 and siman 570 entire siman.
peri-megadim/1:_: Obligated — Taz; Abudraham explains in Orach Chayyim; Avodat Yisrael letter 2 explains further; wrote: be careful in intent and let it be joy of mitzvah — Purim feast, matanot laevyonim, mishloach manot.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: (א) In Shulchan Aruch: mitzvah to increase etc.; see Birkei Yosef in name of one kadosh in responsum: if Purim feast without bread he fulfilled; see Mahari Molcho: one who ate Purim night and meal continued till day and ate some by day fulfilled; see Kaf HaChayyim and Peri Chadash: at night even torch opposite him didn't fulfill; Beit Yosef "like night without torch opposite" means also by day in dark house, but not dark — plainly no lighting needed — lamp in daylight what help? I saw chasidim and men of deed at meal after Minchah lit candles to rejoice till end Bnei Chiya; see Likutei Peri Chadash Terumat HaDeshen s.k. 100: feast by day lights torch for joy and Yom Tov — see there; I didn't find in Terumat HaDeshen; see Mishna Berurah on Sefer Shoneh Halachot; Mor Uktzia: no need to remember Jerusalem destruction at Purim feast since must become intoxicated etc.
levushei-serad/2:_: s.k. 2 and Or Zaru'a 493 — should read siman 570; see Magen Avraham s.k. 8.
